label: r3c3
name: Mirror head, r2c2 recipe, lr 0.002
hypothesis: Same as r2c2, but with the learning rate doubled to 0.002. r2c2's training success first rose only between 25% and 50% of training and was still climbing at the end, so the run is limited by learning speed. Linear decay and gradient clipping should keep the late phase stable. Refuted if the mean is at or below 0.946 or either seed becomes unstable (below 0.85).
last_analysis: The left-right flip of trunk features before the footprint pool head is what makes learning work: without it, scores stay at 0, and a learned column mixer (r1c3) failed. The recipe is the next biggest lever. Two PPO epochs with 64 minibatches and gamma 0.97 lifted the score from about 0.74 to about 0.95 (r2c2 0.946, r3c3 0.949; seeds within 0.03 of each other). Two runs that cut gradient steps had a seed collapse (r1c2 and r3c2, one epoch). Doubling lr to 0.002 sped up early learning: training success was 0.17 at 25% of training versus 0.006. Training success was still rising at the end, so learning speed still limits these runs. The global-context head was no better under the good recipe (0.928). The remaining dev failures are few, and the best runs place almost nothing outside the target (0.10 cells per episode), so the last errors are probably about build order or the final brick. With one round left, I'm making safe, single-change recipe refinements of r3c3.
